identification.summary: UNC5325 is Mandiant's designation for a suspected Chinese cyber espionage operator that exploited CVE-2024-21893 (SSRF in the SAML component) against Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) appliances, reused open-source code, installed custom malware and altered appliance settings to evade detection [S1]. Observed malware: LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA, PITSTOP, PITDOG, PITJET, PITHOOK, plus a BUSHWALK web shell variant [S1]. Mandiant assesses with moderate confidence that UNC5325 is associated with UNC3886, based on TTP and code overlaps in LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA and PITHOOK [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Mandiant saw exploitation of CVE-2024-21893 as early as 2024-01-19 [S1].
identification.notes: UNC5325 is an uncategorized Mandiant cluster, not a Microsoft-named actor; no Microsoft name or MITRE group mapping was found in the sources gathered. Mandiant treats UNC5325 as distinct from UNC5221 (the other China-nexus Ivanti cluster) because the data did not settle whether they are the same [S6]. The UNC3886 association is moderate-confidence and is not a merger of the clusters [S1].

attribution.confidence: Mandiant describes UNC5325 as a suspected China-nexus espionage operator and assesses with moderate confidence an association with UNC3886 [S1]. No government attribution was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Mandiant cites TTP and malware code overlaps between LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA and PITHOOK and malware used by UNC3886 [S1]. UNC3886 is itself described by Mandiant as a suspected China-nexus actor targeting network devices and virtualization technologies [S1].

sectors: Defense industrial base (Ivanti ICS victims across several industries, including the U.S. DIB, per Mandiant's overall Ivanti investigation; not specific to UNC5325) [S1]
Defense, technology and telecommunications (associated cluster UNC3886) [S1]
regions: United States and Asia-Pacific (associated cluster UNC3886) [S1]
targeting.notes: Mandiant's post does not publish a UNC5325 victim list. The DIB reference applies to the broader Ivanti ICS investigation and the sector/region focus applies to UNC3886 [S1]. Targeting is of internet-facing edge appliances (Ivanti ICS) [S1].

capabilities.summary: Exploited CVE-2024-21893 chained with CVE-2024-21887 command injection for unauthenticated access to ICS appliances; validated targets with public tooling (Interactsh) using out-of-band DNS, then performed reconnaissance and in some cases opened a reverse shell [S1]. Used living-off-the-land techniques and abused the legitimate SparkGateway plugin mechanism: PITFUEL loads LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA, which hooks the web process (via PITSOCK), persists across upgrades by appending components to backup/upgrade archives, and attempted (unsuccessfully, because of an encryption key mismatch) to persist through factory reset [S1]. PITDOG injects PITHOOK into the web process using an unmodified open-source Kubo Injector build and relaunches PITSTOP, a backdoor providing shell execution and file read/write over TLS [S1]. A new BUSHWALK Perl web shell variant (arbitrary file read) appeared within 12 hours of Ivanti's 2024-01-31 disclosure, and a user-agent-triggered activate/deactivate technique let the actor evade the Ivanti Integrity Checker Tool by reverting changes between its default two-hour scans [S1]. LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA also functions as a standalone backdoor (command execution, file management, SOCKS proxy, tunneling) [S1].

campaigns.name: Earliest observed CVE-2024-21893 exploitation
campaigns.summary: Mandiant observed exploitation of the SAML SSRF flaw CVE-2024-21893, which Ivanti disclosed on 2024-01-31 as a bypass of its initial mitigation, as early as 2024-01-19 [S1].

campaigns.name: Mass exploitation of CVE-2024-21893 following disclosure
campaigns.summary: Shadowserver reported attacks from more than 170 IPs after disclosure and Rapid7's proof-of-concept of 2024-02-02. Reporting does not attribute this mass exploitation to UNC5325 specifically; Mandiant describes mass exploitation by a small number of China-nexus actors [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: Mandiant publication of UNC5325 activity (Cutting Edge, Part 3)
campaigns.summary: Mandiant disclosed UNC5325 use of CVE-2024-21893, LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA, PITHOOK and related tooling, detection guidance, YARA rules and the moderate-confidence UNC3886 association [S1].

diamond.adversary: Suspected Chinese espionage operator tracked as UNC5325, moderately associated with UNC3886 [S1].
diamond.capability: CVE-2024-21893 chained with CVE-2024-21887; LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA, PITFUEL, PITSOCK, PITDOG, PITHOOK, PITSTOP, PITJET, BUSHWALK; open-source Kubo Injector; Interactsh; living-off-the-land [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: Out-of-band DNS domains via Interactsh for target validation [S1]. Further C2 infrastructure details were not found in the sources gathered.
diamond.victim: Ivanti Connect Secure appliances; Mandiant's wider Ivanti investigation includes the U.S. defense industrial base [S1].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing VPN/edge appliances with limited EDR visibility, and reliance on integrity-check tooling that scans on an interval (default two hours) [S1].

gaps: Victim count, victim identities and exfiltrated data for UNC5325 are not public in the sources gathered [S1].
PITJET is named by Mandiant but not described in the post body [S1].
Sponsor, tasking and objectives are not stated by Mandiant; no government attribution found.
UNC5325 to UNC3886 link is moderate confidence only; relationship to UNC5221 (separate Ivanti cluster) is unresolved [S1][S6].
No Microsoft actor name or MITRE ATT&CK group mapping for UNC5325 was found; the imported MISP entry has no aliases.
Mandiant's post contains minor inconsistencies (an advisory link and an event ID, ERR31903 vs ERR31093); verify against Ivanti advisories before building detections [S1].
Activity after February 2024 was not found; the cluster's current status is unknown.
SecurityWeek, The Hacker News (Ivanti) and Malpedia pages could not be fetched; secondary coverage relied on search summaries.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing VPN/remote-access appliances (Ivanti ICS) used by DIB and defense-adjacent organizations are key cyber terrain; they sit at the boundary and can expose credentials and internal reach [S1]. STEP 2: The battlespace is edge appliances where EDR is limited, and defenders rely on vendor integrity-check tooling that the actor evaded using timed activate/deactivate behavior [S1]. STEP 3: Observed pattern: exploit a newly disclosed mitigation bypass within weeks of the vendor advisory, validate with out-of-band DNS, recon, web shell/backdoor, persistence in upgrade and backup paths, and living-off-the-land use [S1]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued exploitation of the next edge-device vulnerability by this cluster or UNC3886 against defense, technology and telecom targets in the US and Asia-Pacific [S1]. MDCOA is persistence surviving patching, upgrade and reimaging on an unpatched appliance, giving durable access to DIB networks [S1]. Candidate indicators: log events AUT31556 and the saml-server crash event, unexpected files such as /data/pkg/data-backup.tgz modifications, DSUserAgentCap.pm changes, SparkGateway plugin additions, and out-of-band DNS lookups from the appliance [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: inventory Ivanti ICS/Policy Secure assets on supported networks and contractor enclaves, and track vendor advisories and CISA KEV entries for rapid mitigation status [S1][S2]. (2) Authorities: compromised appliances may need to be treated as persistent-compromise cases, since reimaging may not remove implants; coordinate decisions on isolation and rebuild with the system owner and the appropriate cyber defense authority [S1]. (3) Mission assurance: plan for loss of remote access capability when appliances are taken offline and for alternative access paths. (4) Coordination: share indicators and YARA rules with DC3, DIB cybersecurity partners and the owning commands, and keep UNC5325, UNC3886 and UNC5221 distinct in reporting [S1][S6].

provenance.importedSummary: UNC5325 is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage operator that exploited CVE-2024-21893 to compromise Ivanti Connect Secure appliances. UNC5325 leveraged code from open-source projects, installed custom malware, and modified the appliance's settings in order to evade detection and attempt to maintain persistence. UNC5325 has been observed deploying LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA, PITSTOP, PITDOG, PITJET, and PITHOOK. Mandiant identified TTPs and malware code overlaps in LITTLELAMB.WOOLTEA and PITHOOK with malware leveraged by UNC3886. Mandiant assesses with moderate confidence that UNC5325 is associated with UNC3886.
